correctness.rationale: In the Guo–Xu–Zhang A-model convention, Theorems 2.3 and 3.3 and Corollary 4.6 give exactly the signed rational potential and critical numerator used here. With r=p², substitution yields Q/Q_c=(1−Δ)(1−Δ/r)^(−r) and 1−Q/Q_c=(r−1)Δ²/(2r)+O(Δ³). The positive square-root branch is selected on the real interval q∈[0,1/r). To justify the angular-domain transfer explicitly, the inverse polynomial's only finite critical values are 0 and Q_c. The germ q(0)=0 is regular since Q′(0)=1; continuation on the slit plane with [Q_c,∞) and 0 removed has trivial monodromy on this sheet, as the only generator is a small loop about 0. It therefore extends across 0 and is regular at all other points of the convergence circle. There are no other potential poles on this branch: q=1 occurs only over Q=0 on other sheets, and Δ=0 occurs at Q_c. The convergent Puiseux expansion there and coefficient transfer give Q_c^(−d)d^((5g−7)/2)/Γ((5g−5)/2) times the displayed amplitude before the Gamma factor; powers of p and p²−1 simplify as stated. The ψ intersection is positive by the intersection-number recursion, so the radius and eventual sign follow. This is a proof check, not a finite-degree fit.

value.rationale: The coefficient asymptotic is useful to state and the asymptotic problem was well motivated. Once the exact all-genus critical numerator, algebraic potential and critical values of the mirror map are known, the remaining work is a routine singularity-analysis deduction. There is no distinct new estimate, obstruction or invariant beyond the transfer of the already established critical amplitude.
